chunks: Zurarah narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said:

I said to him: A man prostrates while he is wearing a cap or a turban. He said: “If any part of his forehead touches the ground, in the area between his eyebrows and the hairline of his hair, then it has sufficed for him.”

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: it sufficed; it fulfilled the legal requirement
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground which is touched in prostration
key_terms.جَبْهَتِهِ: his forehead, the area relevant for sajdah
key_terms.حَاجِبَيْهِ: his two eyebrows, marking one boundary of the forehead area
key_terms.قَلَنْسُوَةٌ: a cap worn on the head
key_terms.قُصَاصِ شَعْرِهِ: the hairline, marking the upper boundary of the forehead area

ai.seo_question: Is sajdah valid if someone is wearing a cap or turban and only part of the forehead touches the ground?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about sajdah, clarifying that prostration is valid if some part of the forehead touches the ground within the defined area of the forehead. It addresses the case of a person wearing a cap or turban and indicates the minimum required contact for validity.
